metadata.fiscalCycle: CY 2026 Adopted Municipal Budget & User-Friendly Budget
metadata.sourceAgency: City of Clifton Municipal Clerk, CFO & NJ Department of Community Affairs (DLGS)
metadata.documentTitle: 2026 Municipal Data Sheet & Adopted Budget Resolution

governingBody.adoptionVote: Adopted April 21, 2026 (5-2 Vote: Grabowski, Pino, D'Amato, Gibson, Latona voting Aye; Kolodziej, Sadrakula voting Nay)

revenueSources.source: Local Property Tax for Municipal Purposes (including RUT)
revenueSources.description: Portion paid on quarterly municipal property tax bills by Clifton homeowners and commercial property owners

revenueSources.source: Miscellaneous Anticipated Revenues (State Aid, Fees, Grants & Fines)
revenueSources.description: State formula aid (Energy Tax Receipts), construction code permits, municipal court fines, PILOT fees, and shared service revenues
Audited prior-year unreserved municipal fund balance appropriated to stabilize tax rates
Dedicated municipal library levy funding Clifton Main Memorial Library and Allwood Branch operations
Collections from prior-year delinquent municipal taxes, tax sale certificate liens, and statutory penalty interest

majorAppropriations.details: Medical, prescription, and dental coverage for active municipal staff and eligible retirees. Sheet 3b(2) reflects total estimated group health costs of $33.91M, with $4.68M employee Chapter 78 premium cost-sharing contributions.
Salaries and wages ($24,798,000) for sworn Clifton police officers (patrol, detectives, juvenile, traffic, K-9) plus operational expenses ($860,000) for cruisers, fuel, body cameras, and ammunition.
Salaries ($16,805,000) for professional firefighters, captains, lieutenants, and EMTs across 5 fire stations, plus apparatus maintenance, gear, and ambulance supplies ($636,500).

Mandatory employer pension billings from the NJ Division of Pensions and Benefits: $12,111,760 for Police & Firemen's Retirement System (PFRS) and $2,742,598 for Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS).
Principal redemption ($5,240,000) and interest ($1,570,000 bonds, $300,000 notes, $70,905 SENs, $85,000 Green Trust loans) on capital improvement and infrastructure bonds.

Salaries ($5.3M) and operational expenses ($1.39M) for road repair, curbside recycling collection ($1.03M), shade tree maintenance ($743k), vehicle fleet maintenance ($1.43M), and municipal park upkeep ($1.1M).

City Manager executive office, City Clerk (elections/OPRA), City Council, Finance/CFO ($1.22M), Tax Collector ($463k), Tax Assessor ($521k), Legal Counsel ($722k), Engineering ($570k), Personnel ($649k), and MIS Technology ($396k).
Dedicated municipal library tax funding Clifton Main Memorial Library and Allwood Branch library personnel, digital media, collections, and educational programs.
Municipal risk management, comprehensive general liability coverage ($3.5M), and Self-Insurance Trust Fund ($1.3M).

majorAppropriations.category: Statutory Reserve for Uncollected Taxes (RUT — N.J.S.A. 40A:4-40)
majorAppropriations.details: Under NJ cash-basis budgeting statutes, Clifton must guarantee and remit 100% of certified school and county tax levies, requiring a mandatory $4.50M cash overlay reserve based on a 98.70% collection rate.

majorAppropriations.category: Health, Human Services, Senior Services & Recreation
majorAppropriations.details: Clifton Board of Health ($1.45M), municipal recreation and playground programs ($760k), Senior Citizen and Handicapped programs ($490k), Clifton Animal Shelter ($263k), and Human Services ($225k).

majorAppropriations.category: Municipal Court, Land Use & Code Enforcement
majorAppropriations.details: Municipal Court judge, prosecutor, and court administrator ($1.23M), Housing Department ($585k), Planning and Zoning Boards ($347k), Public Defender ($65k), and ABC Board.
Mandatory employer payroll tax contribution matching FICA / Medicare for all eligible municipal employees.
Salaries ($300,000) and supplies/equipment ($280,000) for school crossing guards protecting Clifton Public Schools students at crosswalks across the city.
Official 2026 Budget Sheet 3b(2) documents 116 municipal employees electing health benefits waiver opt-out cash stipends totaling $450,000 annually under N.J.S.A. 40A:10-17.1.

majorAppropriations.category: Dedicated Municipal Sewer Utility Enterprise (Separate Utility Budget)
majorAppropriations.details: Self-liquidating utility enterprise billed separately based on metered water consumption. Appropriates $9,500,000 for Passaic Valley Sewerage Commission (PVSC) regional sewage treatment, $1.76M for local sewer operations, and $2.27M in utility debt service.
